text:
Alex R: Hey team — customer report: streaming (SSE) responses regularly cut off before the final chunk. Client shows a valid sequence of `data: {...}` events then connection closes and there is no final `data: [DONE]` or `finish_reason`. Repro attached below.

Priya S: thanks. Do you have the exact request + headers + model? Also is there a proxy/load balancer in front of the client? Dont paste secret token here.

Alex R: Model: `redwood/gpt-4o-stream-8k` (customer provided), host `api.redwood.ai`. They used an EventSource polyfill on iOS and also tried a server-side curl repro. Token redacted. Repro curl they ran:

```
curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --no-buffer \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-4o-stream-8k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize this long doc"}],"stream":true}'
```

Alex R: Client output shows repeated `data: {"role":"assistant","content":"...partial..."}` lines. Then abruptly: `event: close` (or nothing) and stream connection resets. No `data: [DONE]`.

Mikael: From infra logs for that customer around the same timestamp I see repeated: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `connection reset by peer`. Snippet: 

```
2026-11-17T15:12:03Z nginx[pid]: 2026/11/17 15:12:03 [error] 2345#0: *1023 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.12.2.34, server: api.redwood.ai
```

Priya S: that pattern usually indicates either (1) a client/network disconnect (mobile transitioning networks), (2) a proxy (nginx/ingress) timing out or tearing the connection, or (3) the backend process aborted (OOM or auth/billing forced termination). Check for 401/402/429 entries nearby — midstream 401/402 will sometimes cause connection termination without a neat final JSON.

Alex R: They also reported a prior `401` on an earlier attempt (token refresh race), but not in every case. Could a token expiry midstream cause the server to drop the connection and not emit finish_reason?

Sophia L: We validate tokens at connection start. However, if a billing/quota enforcement or model process dies after the stream started, the model backend might terminate without sending the final `finish_reason`. That will look like truncated output on the client. Check control plane logs for `quota_exceeded` or `billing_block` markers.

Support Bot: Incident flagged: customer_id=cust-824, event=stream-truncation, correlation_id=ci-9f3a.

Alex R: I built a minimal node repro that reproduces truncation by simulating a flaky network (close after N seconds). Node code: 

```
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer REDACTED' } });
es.onmessage = (ev) => {
  console.log('MSG', ev.data);
};
setTimeout(() => {
  // simulate network flap / client reconnect
  es.close();
  console.log('client closed connection');
}, 6200);
```

Alex R: With the above, repeated runs show last event is a partial JSON line and no `[DONE]`/`finish_reason`.

Priya S: repro is useful. Two quick diagnostic asks for the customer: (A) run `curl -i --no-buffer` and capture the full response headers and any trailing status lines, (B) enable verbose logs on the client and paste any `Connection: close`/`RST` traces. Example curl check: 

```
curl -i --no-buffer -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"...","stream":true}'
```

Look for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and confirm last bytes include `data: [DONE]` or `data: {"finish_reason":"stop"}`. If upstream logs show 5xx or `client closed connection`, that points to network/client side close. If control plane shows `billing_block` at the same timestamp, that's our cause.

Mikael: From infra perspective, if upstream process is killed (OOM, cgroups) we will frequently see `upstream prematurely closed connection` followed immediately by no trailing chunk. Also some LB health checks or autoscaler restarts during cold-start might interrupt the model process. For Dedicated customers we see fewer of these.

Alex R: Customer is on Hosted. Any mitigation we can recommend now?

Priya S: short-term suggestions to give customer:
- Implement robust reconnect: if client loses SSE connection, re-open using conversation context and request the missing tail (replay last N tokens).
- Use `--no-buffer`/EventSource streaming and ensure client drains events instead of aborting connection.
- If using a proxy, bump `proxy_read_timeout` and `send_timeout` and disable request buffering. For nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s;`
- Check for 4xx/402/429 around the time of truncation. If found, escalate to billing/auth.

Sophia L: Also ask for the exact `correlation_id` from the customer logs (we can map it to control plane traces). If model process OOM/kill, send us the model name + input size + approximate tokens/sec so runtime can simulate.

Mikael: Small infra trick: if connection closes due to backend kill we sometimes send a final `event: error\ndata: {"type":"internal_error","message":"backend terminated"}\n\n` but not always (race conditions). So absence of any final event doesn't uniquely identify the cause. Need logs.

Alex R: captured curl output sample (trimmed):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
...
data: {"role":"assistant","content":"First chunk..."}
data: {"role":"assistant","content":"Second chunk..."}
<connection reset by peer>
```

Priya S: that `<connection reset by peer>` plus upstream logs is pretty indicative of a client or intermediate closing the socket. If they can reproduce without network flaps (steady desktop with wired connection) and still get truncation then escalate.

Alex R: Next steps: I'll ask the customer to run the curl `-i` check and share the `correlation_id`. I'll also request platform logs around the timestamp. I told them to enable token refresh safe guards so they don't rotate tokens midstream.

Sophia L: If they come back with `billing_block` or `quota_exceeded`, route to billing. If logs show model process crash, I'll engage eng-runtime with the reproducer and model details.

Priya S: I'll create a short KB: "SSE partial/truncated output — check proxies, token refresh, billing/quota, and client-side disconnects" and include sample curl and Node EventSource snippets.

Support Bot: Created ticket INC-2026-824 (linked). Adding `sse`, `streaming`, `investigating` tags.

Alex R: Thanks team — I'll update once I have the curl output + correlation_id. :thumbsup:
